samples.question: This picture shows one moth from above: a pale grey wing silhouette printed with small filled round spots that all share one colour. Two small dark grey squares, one beyond the head and one beyond the tail, mark the two ends of the moth's mirror line; the mirror line is the straight line through the centres of those two squares. Call a spot paired when another spot sits at its mirror position across that line, and unpaired when no spot sits there. In this picture every spot is either mirrored exactly by another spot or has a clearly empty mirror position, no spot lies on the mirror line, and at most three spots are unpaired. The two wings need not carry the same number of spots, and the mirror line need not be upright. How many spots are unpaired? Answer with exactly one of: 0, 1, 2, 3.
